checkpoint_review: I have re-evaluated the 'Whiskers' checkpoint. While the Router marked this as 'not present' due to resolution, my independent review confirms that even at this resolution, sea lion whiskers typically cast distinct shadows or appear as dark lines against the snout. Their total absence is an anatomical omission consistent with AI smoothing, not just low fidelity. I maintain the 'Missing' verdict. Regarding 'Fur', the texture is indeed waxy/plastic-like, but the color and general distribution match the taxonomy. I will keep it as 'Checked' but heavily penalize in authenticity. The 'Hind flippers' are genuinely occluded; marking as N/A is correct. All other positive checkpoints (ears, crest, body shape) are visually verified and robust.
authenticity_review: My initial authenticity score of 2.85 was too lenient given the severity of the texture artifact. The 'waxy/plastic' sheen on the sea lion is a fundamental failure of material rendering for a furry mammal, affecting the entire subject, not just a局部 area. This is more severe than the 'slight compression' noted by the perceptual auditor. The fusion at the tail/rock interface is also more pronounced upon closer inspection—the boundary lacks a clean depth discontinuity. Combined with the missing whiskers (anatomical realism failure), the image feels distinctly synthetic. I am lowering the score to reflect that while the geometry is good, the surface realism is poor.
